verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The paper's display is stated in Lean, for the full curl-corrected covariance and with no hypotheses, as `ActualInitialMean.matched_fluxes`; the only encoding choice is that '+ higher-order terms' is membership in a strictly higher mean class rather than an additive remainder named in the statement. Matching of the parts, each opened in its source file: `strip = BaseContextAssembly.nativeStrip ActualPrimary.nominal ActualPrimary.standardRegion` (ActualInitialMean.lean:27-28), the same strip as in ActualPrimaryCovariance; `seed B N0 = bandSeed (ActualPrimary.activeLabels standardRegion B N0) primaryPiece (baseError B)` (line 43-44) with `primaryPiece l = ActualPrimary.piece standardRegion l.2 l.1` (line 37-38), the same primary family as `tangentCovariance B N0`; and `bandSeed_covariance` (CorrectionInitialization.lean:1114-1118) gives `(bandSeed labels pieces e).covariance i j = bilinearCovariance (fieldSum labels fun l => (pieces l).velocity) (…) i j` by `rfl` — the piece's full `velocity`, i.e. the curl corrections are inside the left-hand side, not only the tangential part. `bilinearCovariance u u i j = angularAverage (u_i u_j)` (CorrectionState.lean:73-78) is the paper's ⟨·⟩_θ and `StateMomentBalances.meanBar` (StateMomentBalances.lean:23) is its ⟨·⟩_Y, so the two left-hand sides are literally ⟨w̃_r w̃_θ⟩ and ⟨w̃_r w̃_z⟩ (index 0 = radial, 1 = θ, 2 = z, as in `chart_physical_leading` and as confirmed by `angularBase_physical`/`axialBase_physical`, BaseContextAssembly.lean:470-478). On the right, `(commonContext B).virtualTheta/.virtualAxial` are the two components of `BaseContextAssembly.virtualStress` (BaseContextAssembly.lean:467-468), the annulus-supported target stress. The version whose right-hand side is literally the paper's T is `averagedDefect_meanClass`: `averagedDefect B N0 i = meanBar (tangentCovariance B N0 0 i.succ) - leadingStress i` with `leadingStress i` the i-th component of `leadingVirtualStress` = T, and the theorem puts that difference in MeanClass β for *every* real β — the defect is supported on the finite retained band prefix and vanishes identically past band `(choice B N0).prepared.N + 1` (`averagedDefect_zero_tail`, line 748), so for the Y-averaged tangential covariance the paper's identity holds with an error smaller than any power. The curl-correction part of the higher-order terms is the second clause of `ActualInitialMean.covariance_bounds`: full minus tangential covariance in MeanClass 3/2 - κ with κ = 1/100000 (ChartScales.lean:24), strictly above the leading class 1 of `leadingStress_meanClass` (ActualPrimaryCovariance.lean:824) — the paper's 'smaller by positive powers of q'. Recovery of the display as the paper writes it (right-hand side T, not the full virtual stress): add `averagedDefect_meanClass B N0 i (3/2 - kappa)` to the Y-average of `covariance_bounds B N0 .2`, the Y-average preserving mean class by `ActualInitialMean.meanBar_mem` (line 355, via `LocalSignedRequest.meanClass_liftedTorusAverage`). The one convention worth recording, not a gap: `matched_fluxes` states the right-hand side as the full virtual stress rather than its leading term T, the two differing by the MeanClass-2 `context_higher_stress_classes` invoked inside `tangent_virtual_bar_meanClass` (line 893).
